connector: Hoo! The last week of 4th grade ELA. This week you polish your comparison paragraph, look back at how you’ve grown, and celebrate. Today: make your best paragraph even better.

a.raw: matthew cuthbert i believe that child has bewitched you said marilla
a.fixed: “Matthew Cuthbert, I believe that child has bewitched you!” said Marilla.
a.why: Marilla’s real words (Anne of Green Gables, Ch. 3): a comma after the name of the person spoken to; the exclamation point inside the quotation marks.

b.raw: i revised my paragraph and i fixed three spelling mistakes
b.fixed: I revised my paragraph, and I fixed three spelling mistakes.
b.why: Capital I both times; a comma before and joins two complete thoughts; a period ends it.

scholar.journal-q1: … and say which revision helped most.
scholar.journal-q2: … and give the before and after for one.
scholar.journal-q3: … and say what would raise it one level.

copia.seed: I grew as a reader this year.
eg: Book by book, I grew as a reader this year.
I stretched as a reader this year.
I grew as a reader this year, from August to May.

notes.wgrd: Reflect on how your reading habits have grown: who you were as a reader in August, who you are now, and the proof.
vocab: To change your writing to make the ideas better.
To check writing for mistakes in capitals, usage, punctuation and spelling.
A collection of your best work.
To think back on something and what it taught you.
notes.wordParts: Every base from the year: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script, rupt, duct, form, press, tain, lev, plus prefixes like pre-, re-, trans-, inter-.
notes.grammar: Spiral review: capitals, commas, quotation marks, complete sentences. Read your sentence out loud and check each mark has a job.
notes.spelling: Spiral review: drop the silent e, change y to i, double the last consonant when the beat is on the last syllable, and spell each word part the same way every time.

transcripts.welcome: Hoo! It’s Opti. This is the last week of 4th grade ELA. Today’s question: what makes a strong comparison paragraph, and how can you make yours even stronger?
transcripts.read: Read your paragraph as if someone else wrote it. Is the theme clear in the first sentence? Is there proof from both books? Change one sentence to make it sharper, then check capitals, usage, punctuation and spelling.
transcripts.morphology: You know more roots than you think. Some you haven’t used yet. Try putting them to work: press means push, tain means hold, lev means lift. Find a word with one of them and use it in your own writing.
